subject: Evidence package for private deployment outbound controls (Acme Health)
body:
From: Tom Harper <tom.harper@acmehealth.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound controls evidence for private endpoint deployment

Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week. Security wants a concise package showing exactly how Redwood's private endpoint (VPC) deployment prevents uncontrolled outbound connections from our environment. We need concrete artefacts we can hand to our network/security team and evidence we can attach to our audit. At minimum we'd like:

- IP ranges (and explanation of regional/ephemeral addresses) that must be permitted from the private nodes
- Ports / protocols that need outbound access (and which are required/optional)
- If any TLS SNI or hostname allowlisting is required (plus cert fingerprints or CA chain details)
- Whether mTLS is used between customer connector and control plane, and where
- Guidance on proxying / transparent proxy support vs NAT egress (what headers change)
- An example pcap / sample session that shows a healthy request sequence (redacted)
- A short operational checklist for incident responders (how to verify a blocked flow)

Can you provide a single ZIP or drive folder with those items? Also, if you have an attestation or runbook signoff we can include in our internal package that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harper
Head of Infrastructure Security
Acme Health

-----Original Message-----

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: Tom Harper <tom.harper@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound controls evidence for private endpoint deployment

Tom —

Appreciate the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Customer Ops) and Laura (Networking/Private Deploy) so we can bundle an evidence packet.

Quick note on scope: Redwood private endpoints rely on a small set of well-defined outbound channels from the runtime/control connector. We can provide the exact IPv4/IPv6 blocks we expect customers to permit, a port/protocol matrix, and a sample PCAP of a single session (sanitized). We also have an internal safelist assertion PDF our compliance team signs for private installs.

Plan: Marissa to produce the ops checklist and the sanitized pcap; Laura to confirm the IP/port matrix; I'll compile and send a Drive link and a single PDF attestation. Target delivery: next Thu (2027-03-18).

Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 10:22 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:

Neha / Tom —

I'll own the ops checklist and the sample pcap. A couple of notes for your SOC: we intentionally minimize outbound DNS and control-plane chatter by batching heartbeats and using a single TLS egress endpoint per region. That means:

- Customers only need to allow the control-plane IPs (we'll provide current list) and outbound TCP/443.
- If you terminate TLS inspection and rewrite SNI, you must preserve the Server Name our runtime expects (we can provide SNI values).
- For customers using a corporate proxy, we support CONNECT with proxy auth; we can also provide a manifest of headers that may be added by proxies so you can map flows.

Attachments I'll include: egress-config-snippet.yaml (how the connector binds and uses outbound sockets), and a CSV of the IP list. We'll sanitize PCAP payloads.

Proposed timeline: send initial bundle Wed 3/17 EOD PT, final attestation Thu 3/18. If Acme needs earlier for procurement, let me know.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 11:05 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:

Tom / Neha / Marissa —

I've verified the current runtime egress footprint for the US region as of 2027-03-17. Summary (high level):

- IPv4: 34.120.88.0/22, 34.122.96.0/23 (subject to rotation; see note)
- IPv6: 2600:1400::/36
- Ports: 443 (TLS), 53 (optional DNS if using local resolver), 123 (NTP if not using host sync)
- TLS: outbound to control.redwood-inference.com; TLS 1.2+; we publish the public cert chain (sha256 fingerprint: 3f:ab:...:d2)
- mTLS: optional for private control-plane peering; customers who require mutual auth can configure client certs (we can exchange a CSR/issued cert during onboarding)

Rotation note: ephemeral egress IPs are possible for autoscaled worker pools. For guaranteed static exit IPs we offer a managed NAT overlay (Dedicated/Private tier) — if you require absolute static outbound addresses we should plan a dedicated NAT appliance.

I'll add these to the CSV and include a brief paragraph in the ops checklist about verifying NAT vs ephemeral behavior.

Laura Bennett
Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

---- Forwarded message ----
From: procurement@acmehealth.com
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound controls evidence for private endpoint deployment

Neha / Marissa —

Two procurement items: 1) Can you confirm whether the safelist assertion is sufficient for our auditors (they prefer a signed PDF), and 2) can you provide a short statement about data exfil prevention at the egress boundary (we need a one-paragraph blurb for our SOW).

Procurement Team
Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 10:04 AM neha.kapoor@redwood.com wrote:

Procurement / Tom / Marissa —

1) Yes — we will provide a signed safelist assertion PDF. That doc includes a high-level statement of controls and is stamped by our compliance lead.

2) Short blurb for SOW (draft):

"Redwood Inference private deployments operate with a least-privilege outbound posture. Runtime components only initiate outbound connections to a documented set of control-plane endpoints. Optional managed NAT appliances or static egress pools are available for customers requiring fixed exit addresses. Customers may combine network-level allowlisting with proxying or TLS inspection; where TLS inspection is performed, Redwood provides SNI and certificate fingerprints and supports mTLS for mutual authentication to prevent unauthorized third-party interception. Logs and trace evidence for outbound requests are available for incident response and regular audits."

I'll attach the signed safelist assertion and the sanitized PCAP. Final bundle coming Thu 3/18.

Neha Kapoor

-----Message from Redwood attachments-----
Attachments: egress-config-snippet.yaml, egress-iplist-v20270317.csv

On Thu, 18 Mar 2027 at 16:05 Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:

Tom / Security / Procurement —

Attached is the evidence bundle we discussed. Contents: 

- redwood-safelist-assertion.pdf (signed by Compliance lead)
- egress-iplist-v20270317.csv (current IPs and rotation policy notes)
- egress-traffic-sample.pcap (sanitized single-session capture showing TLS handshake and control request)
- egress-config-snippet.yaml (connector config excerpt showing outbound binding and optional mTLS settings)

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3EgR-REDWOOD-ACME-EGRESS
JIRA ticket created for follow-up verification: JIRA-SEC-4492

Operational checklist (short):
1) Verify your firewall permits egress to the listed IPs on TCP/443.
2) Confirm SNI passthrough or configure SNI allowlist to match control.redwood-inference.com.
3) If you use a corporate proxy, ensure CONNECT preserves the Host header; map proxy-added headers as needed.
4) To confirm flows, pull a 5-min packet capture at the time of a test run; compare destination IP and SNI to the CSV.
5) If you require static egress, notify us to schedule a dedicated NAT overlay deployment (lead time ~2 weeks).

If you'd like a short live session with our network engineer to walk through the PCAP and checklist, we're available Fri 3/19 or Mon 3/22.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
